summary: Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Rinzin Thargyal works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Magister at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisor Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later holding a post at the University of Bristol around 2005.

Rita M. Gross was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1974–1979) and the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire (1979–2013).
Rizong Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College from around 1984 to 1995.

Rob Linrothe specializes in history/archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD at the University of Chicago, he held posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009), the Rubin Museum of Art (2002–2004), and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and the University of London. He held posts at the University of Zimbabwe and the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal and Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He held posts at Amherst College, Harvard University, Columbia University, and the American Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Robert Aitken was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaii, UC Berkeley, and Ryutaku-ji, with teachers including D. T. Suzuki and Soen Nakagawa, and held a post at the University of Hawaii.
Robert Alan Goodding is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.
Robert B. Ekvall worked in Tibetology. He held appointments at the University of Chicago (around 1953–1958), the University of Washington (1958), and the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture.
Robert Barnett is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Cambridge from 1973 to 1976. He served as a professor at Columbia University from approximately 1998 to 2017.

Robert Caesar Childers worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College and under Yataramulle Dhammarama, later holding posts at the India Office, University College London, and the University of London.

Robert Chalmers was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Oriel College from around 1877 to 1881 and later served as Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge, from 1924 to 1931.

Robert Chambers worked in Indology and other fields, having studied at Lincoln College. He held positions at the University of Oxford (1762–1777), the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1789–1798), and the Asiatic Society (1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Christ Church, he served in the Secret Intelligence Service (1943–1952) and as Spalding Professor at the University of Oxford (1952–1974).

Robert DeCaroli is an art historian and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his degrees at UCLA under Robert L. Brown. He has held teaching posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount University, and George Mason University.
Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford. He held posts at the University of Kerala and the Université catholique de Louvain.
Robert Duquenne worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Between 1974 and 1998, he held posts at Hōbōgirin and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kusan Sunim and completed his PhD at UC Berkeley. He served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, from 1986 to 2016.
